title: Prompting vs RAG vs Fine Tuning

scenes.text: So you want an AI that really knows your business. [1] Should you write a better prompt, use RAG, or fine tune a model? [2] Let's settle this once and for all.

First, what exactly is fine tuning? [1] It means training an existing model a little more, on your own examples, so it learns a new style or a new skill. [2] It needs a lot of examples, [3] it changes how the model behaves, [4] and it costs both time and money.

data.definition: Extra training on your own examples, so the model learns a style or skill.

scenes.text: Here's an easy way to think about it. Imagine a new employee. [1] Prompting is like giving them clear instructions for today's task. [2] RAG is like handing them the company handbook, so they can look things up. [3] And fine tuning is like sending them on a training course, for a few months.

data.heading: Think: a new employee
items: Send them on a training course

scenes.text: Here's your cheat sheet. [1] We have three options. [2] Setup cost, prompting is basically free, RAG is low, and fine tuning is high. [3] Need fresh or private information? RAG wins. [4] Need a special style or format? Fine tuning wins. [5] And to get started quickly, prompting takes just minutes. [6] So here's the rule of thumb. Start with prompts, add RAG for knowledge, and fine tune for behaviour.

data.heading: The cheat sheet
data.note: Prompt first → RAG for knowledge → fine-tune for behaviour

scenes.text: Let's look at some real examples. [1] A startup writing social media captions? Good prompts are enough. [2] A law firm answering from thousands of case files? That's RAG. [3] And a telecom company that wants replies in its exact brand tone, every single time? That's fine tuning.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think fine tuning is the best way to teach a model new facts. [2] Usually, it's not. Fine tuning is great for style and behaviour. But for facts that keep changing, RAG is cheaper, and much easier to update.

data.myth: Fine-tuning is the best way to add new facts.
data.fact: Fine-tuning shapes style and behaviour. For changing facts, RAG is cheaper and easier to update.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! Your prices change every week, and your chatbot must always know the latest ones. Which approach should you use? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] It's RAG! Just update the documents, and the answers update instantly.

Let's recap. [1] Prompting is giving instructions, so always start there. [2] RAG adds knowledge that stays fresh. [3] Fine tuning teaches style and behaviour.
